correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every ternary relation atom on two variable names to equality/identity/squaring/inverse predicates; each nonidentity element in a prime-exponent group has an explicitly classified finite set of possible second-pebble atomic types. Those sets are uniform in each of the six rows, giving a permanent two-pebble strategy. Four FO2 sentences realize six distinct truth vectors; the unitriangular example and FO3 separator are explicit. Two programs verified full atomic profiles and all single-pebble transition types for eleven groups, including nonabelian groups; finite checks corroborate but do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of the ordinary two-variable theories for a natural broad class of finite groups that contains nonabelian groups of unbounded size. The merger of noncyclic exponent-five groups with every prime exponent at least seven, and the sharp two-to-three-variable noncommutativity boundary for same-order abelian/nonabelian examples, are substantive structural findings beyond the special cyclic-prime case. Their significance lies in precise expressibility limitations, not in code, correctness, or non-retrieval alone.
